s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of neurological deficits with reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan
key_facts: 60-year-old woman
Recently diagnosed with HIV
Not yet on antiretroviral therapy
One-day history of reduced consciousness, aphasia, and urinary incontinence
Two-day history of dry cough, drenching night sweats, and weight loss
No fever, headache, neck stiffness, visual disturbances, photophobia, or seizures
Wasted appearance with weight of 40 kg
Afebrile with blood pressure 120/74 mmHg, pulse 66 beats/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14/15 with dysarthria
CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3
Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320

shortlist.label: Cryptococcal meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive serum cryptococcal antigen test and multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple ring-enhancing lesions on brain CT scan, consistent with toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan, which could be consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with severe neurological deficits and white matter lesions on brain CT scan, which could be consistent with PML

shortlist.label: Cerebral nocardiosis
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised patient with multiple enhancing nodular white matter lesions on brain CT scan, which could be consistent with nocardiosis

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive serum cryptococcal antigen test with a titer of 1:320, a very low CD4 count of 6 cells/mm^3, and symptoms consistent with central nervous system infection, such as reduced consciousness and aphasia, which are highly suggestive of cryptococcal meningitis.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While toxoplasmosis is a common opportunistic infection in HIV patients, the positive serum cryptococcal antigen test points more directly to cryptococcal meningitis.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition is less likely given the presence of a positive cryptococcal antigen test and the acute presentation of symptoms.

rejected.label: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, which typically presents with more gradual onset of focal neurological deficits.

rejected.label: Cerebral nocardiosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the case that would suggest cerebral nocardiosis, such as a history of lung disease or specific imaging findings consistent with this diagnosis.
